input.question: Why am I more tired on some mornings than others even if I get around the same sleep every night?
input.ground_truth: It's all about your sleep cycle. You can be sleeping nearly the same amount every night but waking up during different phases of sleep can effect your sleepiness level. There are clocks designed to wake you up at the perfect point in your sleep cycle. Now this may mean that you wake up a little earlier or later than you intended to but you will feel more rested if you wake at the right point in your sleep cycle.

Okay! Imagine you have a toy car, and sometimes you can push it and it goes really far and fast, but other times, even if you push it the same way, it only goes a little bit before you get tired.

Your body is a little like that toy car. When you sleep, your body is resting and getting ready to go. But sometimes, even if you sleep the same amount every night, your body might feel more tired or less tired in the morning. This can happen because of things like:

- What you did the day before (if you played a lot or felt worried or sad, your body might be more tired)
- If you ate something good or not so good for breakfast the day before
- If you were sick a little bit, even if you didn’t know it
- If you dreamed a lot, your brain might feel more tired

So, even if you sleep the same number of hours, sometimes your body just needs a little more energy in the morning, and other times it feels ready to go!
